Communication & Nurse–Patient Relationship

Nurse–patient communication, therapeutic relationship, phases and barriers.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the nurse–patient relationship
  • List phases of the relationship
  • State barriers to communication and how to overcome them

In simple words

The nurse–patient relationship is a professional, trusting relationship built to help the patient meet health goals. It is different from a friendship — it has boundaries and a purpose.

Communication is the heart of this relationship. Good communication helps assessment, teaching and comfort.

Phases of the relationship (Peplau)

Phase What happens
Pre-interaction Nurse prepares before meeting the patient
Orientation Nurse and patient meet; roles and goals are set
Working Patient’s needs are identified and met
Termination Relationship ends when goals are met

Therapeutic communication techniques

  • Active listening — focus fully on the patient.
  • Open questions — “How does the pain feel?”
  • Silence — give the patient time to think.
  • Reflection — “You seem worried about the surgery.”
  • Clarification — “I am not sure I understand; can you say more?”

Barriers to communication

  • Language difference, noise, lack of time.
  • Patient fear, pain or unconsciousness.
  • Nurse being rushed or judgmental.
  • Medical jargon the patient does not understand.

🔴 Professional boundaries

The nurse–patient relationship is professional, not a friendship. It has boundaries, a purpose and ends when goals are met.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Build trust — introduce yourself, keep promises, be honest.
  • Use therapeutic techniques — listen, ask open questions, reflect feelings.
  • Watch barriers — use an interpreter, reduce noise, avoid jargon.
  • Respect privacy — talk where others cannot overhear.
  • End well — summarise what was achieved and say goodbye clearly.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. The nurse–patient relationship is professional, trusting and goal-directed.
  2. Peplau’s phases: pre-interaction, orientation, working, termination.
  3. Therapeutic techniques: active listening, open questions, silence, reflection, clarification.
  4. Communication barriers: language, noise, fear, pain, jargon, being rushed.
  5. Professional boundaries separate the relationship from friendship.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Orientation sets roles and goals with the patient.
  2. Working phase meets the patient’s identified needs.
  3. Reflection means repeating the patient’s feeling back.

📌 Memory trick

Phases: P.O.W.T. — Pre-interaction, Orientation, Working, Termination. Say “pow-t”.

60-second revision

  • Relationship = professional, trusting, goal-directed.
  • Phases: pre-interaction → orientation → working → termination.
  • Techniques: listen, open questions, silence, reflection, clarification.
  • Barriers: language, noise, fear, pain, jargon.
  • Boundaries: not a friendship.

Test yourself

The nurse–patient relationship is:

Answer: B. It is a professional relationship with boundaries and a purpose.

Peplau's first phase is:

Answer: C. Pre-interaction is when the nurse prepares before meeting the patient.

An open question is:

Answer: B. Open questions start with how, what, when, where or why.

Reflection in communication means:

Answer: B. Reflection shows you heard the patient's feeling ('You seem worried').

A barrier to communication is:

Answer: B. Jargon the patient does not understand blocks communication.
